requirements.requirement: Kernel is configured to boot with audit=1 (kernel command line parameter)
requirements.summary: Baseline captured showing audit=1 was absent from /proc/cmdline and grubby --info=DEFAULT. grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="audit=1" was run and verified present in grubby default args, both /boot/loader/entries/*.conf files (normal and rescue), and /etc/kernel/cmdline.

A live reboot was performed on node1 (setsid-backgrounded reboot with immediate ack, confirmed by subsequent connection timeouts). Boot identity changed from 739c9792-2418-47cc-a875-95b27428f3fc to b3721708-41be-4eb1-89e0-f1c9588a7d77 (also confirmed independently by fixed global before_prepare/after_executor snapshots), and uptime -s shows a new boot time. Post-reboot /proc/cmdline contains audit=1, auditctl -s reports 'enabled 1', and grubby --info=DEFAULT still shows audit=1, directly demonstrating the healthy pre-state, the disruption, and the recovered/persisted state.

overall_summary: The executor correctly and persistently applied audit=1 to node1's kernel boot parameters via grubby (covering both the normal and rescue boot entries and /etc/kernel/cmdline), then performed an actual reboot to validate persistence. Boot identity change was independently confirmed by both executor commands and the fixed global lifecycle snapshots, and post-reboot verification directly showed audit=1 in /proc/cmdline, auditctl reporting the audit subsystem enabled, and grubby's default entry still containing audit=1. Both material outcomes (configuration applied, persistence across reboot) are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence and no hygiene concerns.
limitations: Only one boot/kernel entry existed on node1 so grubby --update-kernel=ALL applied to a single entry (plus rescue); multi-kernel persistence across several kernel versions was not exercised, though this reflects the actual system state rather than an evidence gap.
auditd (the userspace daemon) was observed inactive post-reboot; this is outside the task's scope (kernel boot parameter only) but is noted for completeness.

operational_hygiene.summary: Only two state-changing actions occurred: the required grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="audit=1" (cmd-a9922c3989424e1d), directly satisfying the task, and the required reboot (cmd-f6bb728519914328), needed to demonstrate persistence. Both are clearly tied to material task outcomes. No unnecessary mutations, no leftover residue (systemd-private tmp dirs under /tmp changed only due to the reboot regenerating per-boot service sandboxes, which is expected OS behavior, not executor-caused residue), no failed services (none before or after), package manager healthy both before and after, and listening sockets unchanged in substance (same sshd/chronyd ports, just new PIDs after reboot). auditd.service being inactive post-reboot is pre-existing/unrelated to the task, which only required the kernel boot parameter, not the auditd daemon.
